name: MotionNative (exported from root as `Motion`)

stories.quality: Template stub: description 'A glass morphism motionnative component.', empty argTypes/args, 'Variants' story renders a single default instance. Shows none of the 7 types, hover/click triggers, or physics.

material_impl: None (pure motion wrapper). Emits class hooks motion-element/motion-fade/... (MotionNative.tsx:355-370) that have no CSS definitions anywhere in src (rg '.motion-element' in *.css -> 0 hits).
motion: Web Animations API via element.animate (MotionNative.tsx:285-287) plus an optional rAF spring (useMultiSpring, :95-98). Reduced motion read via matchMedia in useEffect (:101-118) and respected (shouldAnimate :120). Defects: (1) delay applied twice — setTimeout(delay) at :325 and timing.delay at :279, so delay=300 waits 600ms; (2) physics mode is effectively a no-op: spring starts at {opacity:1,x:0,y:0} (:96) and targets parsed from the 'to' keyframe are also opacity 1 / translate(0,0) (:257-271), so nothing moves; (3) mount animation runs after first paint, so content flashes visible then jumps to opacity 0 and fades in (FOUC); (4) animateOnHover stopAnimation cancels on mouseleave (:308-310) so content snaps back to non-animated state; (5) useEffect deps omit type/direction/keyframes (:331).
a11y: Neutral wrapper div; onClick on a div with no role/keyboard path when animateOnClick is used. Reduced-motion honored by default (respectReducedMotion=true).
api: forwardRef with manual ref merging (:344-354); className/style passthrough, but style is overwritten by physics transform when physics=true (:336-339). Prop API (type/direction/duration ms/easing string/physics/loop/repeat/fillMode) is completely different from MotionFramer (preset/easing enum/animateOnScroll) yet both are exported under the name `Motion` in different entry points.
ssr: 'use client'; window access only in effect. SSR-safe, but initial server HTML is the final visual state, then client jumps to frame 0 (hydration flash).
fake_complexity: 'physics' is a fake: spring never has a non-trivial target. 'elastic'/'bounce' are plain keyframes, fine.
target: single Motion primitive built on MotionFramer + shared useReducedMotion (src/hooks/useReducedMotion.ts)
justification: A second, hand-rolled motion engine with a fake physics path, a double-applied delay and a mount flash. Worse, src/index.ts:16 exports it as `Motion` while `export * from './primitives'` (src/index.ts:1125) and src/primitives/index.ts:91 export MotionFramer as `Motion` — the explicit root export shadows the star, so `import { Motion } from 'aura-glass'` and `import { Motion } from 'aura-glass/primitives'` resolve to two components with incompatible props, and the root `MotionProps` type (from MotionFramer, primitives/index.ts:83) does not describe the root `Motion`. Internal components (GlassMagneticButton, GlassSelectCompound) import the MotionFramer `Motion`. Delete it and point the root `Motion` at the single framer-based primitive with a deprecation alias.

name: MotionFramer (also Motion / GlassMotion via primitives index)

stories.quality: Template stub identical to MotionNative's; default preset is 'none' so the story animates nothing.

material_impl: None. Class hook 'motion-primitive' (:275) has no CSS.
motion: framer-motion variants with 10 presets (:172-213); presets are restrained and tasteful (12-16px slides, 0.96 scale). Reduced motion: state defaults to true and is resolved in an effect (:235-250). Critical defect: because `reduced` is true on the first render, `initial` is undefined at mount (:277-281); framer-motion only honours `initial` on mount, so when `reduced` flips to false the element is already at its resting values and animateOnMount produces NO visible animation for anyone. Only animateOnScroll (whileInView) and animateOnHover actually work. Also ~150 lines of runtime sanitizers (coerceBackgroundKey/normalizeTransitions, :73-170, :297-348) recursively copy every motion prop on every render to paper over callers passing CSS-ish easing strings and `background` shorthands.
a11y: Reduced-motion default-safe (no animation until preference known). No semantics of its own.
api: forwardRef; className/style passthrough. Declares `as`, `type`, `direction` in MotionProps (:39-42) but never destructures or implements them — they leak into motion.div as invalid DOM attributes (`as="section"`, `type="slide"`). Strips a stray `consciousness` prop (:301) — evidence of upstream prop leakage being patched downstream. Easing enum uses CSS names, durations in ms; differs from MotionNative.
ssr: 'use client'; matchMedia in effect only; hard static import of framer-motion although framer-motion is an optional peer (package.json:396-398) and this module is reachable from the root barrel (src/index.ts:15).
fake_complexity: No fake claims, but 'animateOnMount' is a silent no-op as described.
justification: This is the right foundation (framer-motion, small calm presets, reduced-motion-first), and internal components already depend on it, so it should become the one Motion primitive. But mount animations are broken by the reduced=true bootstrap; fix by using framer's own `useReducedMotion`/`MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"` and always passing `initial`. Implement or delete `as`/`type`/`direction`, delete the recursive prop sanitizers (fix callers instead), move presets to the shared motion tokens in presets.ts, and give it real stories that show each preset.

name: ReducedMotionProvider

stories.quality: Stub; Default story has no children (renders nothing); described as 'A glass morphism reducedmotionprovider component.'

material_impl: n/a (non-visual)
motion: Wraps MotionConfig and maps matchMedia to reducedMotion 'always' | 'never' (:29). Re-implements what framer-motion does natively with reducedMotion="user". Initial state false (:10) means reduced-motion users get full animation on the first render before the effect runs — the opposite bootstrap of MotionFramer. Forcing 'never' also overrides any user-agent preference framer would otherwise detect.
a11y: Intent is accessibility; implementation has a first-frame leak and is functionally inferior to MotionConfig reducedMotion="user".
api: Children only; default export only. Not exported from src/index.ts, src/primitives/index.ts, or src/primitives/motion/index.ts — dead code apart from its story.
target: MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" inside the library's root provider / MotionPreferenceContext
justification: Unexported, unused, and strictly worse than one line of framer-motion config. One of at least four parallel reduced-motion mechanisms (plus ~149 files doing ad-hoc matchMedia). Remove and fold the behaviour into the single motion preference provider.

name: OptimizedGlassCore (root alias OptimizedGlass; also GlassOptimized)

stories.quality: Default, ElevationLevels, IntentVariants, PerformanceTiers, HighPerformance, Showcase — the only real story set in this shard.

tests: none dedicated in src/primitives (consumed by ~180 files, so indirectly exercised)
material_impl: Shared primitive: createGlassStyle (src/core/mixins/glassMixins.ts:41) -> glassTokenUtils.buildSurfaceStyles(intent, elevation, tier) — token-driven background, backdrop-filter (both spellings), border and shadow. This is the canonical material path and is good. Hard-coded: radius scale in px (4/8/12/16/9999, :227-240) instead of radius tokens; glowColor default rgba(255,255,255,0.5) (:143) which is never used.
motion: Transitions come from createGlassStyle (`all ...ms ease-out` — animating `all` on a backdrop-filter surface is expensive). Hover lift / press / sheen via CSS classes (glass-lift-on-hover, glass-press, glass-hover-sheen exist in src/styles/glass.css). No JS motion.
a11y: Polymorphic `as` lets callers pick semantics. interactive=true adds cursor:pointer and user-select:none but no role/tabIndex/keyboard — interactive glass divs are mouse-only unless callers add semantics. focusRing relies on CSS :focus-visible.
api: forwardRef typed as React.ElementRef<any> (:133) — polymorphic typing is effectively lost. ~30 props of which many are accepted and silently ignored: glowColor, glowIntensity, hover, animation, optimization, hardwareAcceleration, intensity, depth, tint, border, blur, variant, lighting (destructured at :142-160 and never used); caustics/chromatic/parallax/refraction/adaptive/magnet/cursorHighlight only become data-* attributes (:299-305) with no implementation. Props are destructured twice (:136-175 and :245-269) plus a regex delete of glass* keys (:273-277) to stop upstream leakage. `tier` default 'high' is overloaded to mean 'auto-detect' (:181, :190).
ssr: 'use client'. SSR-safe by starting at tier 'medium' then switching after mount (:178-207) — causes a post-hydration restyle (blur/shadow change) on every high-tier device. Uses cached detectDevice (src/utils/deviceCapabilities.ts:117-190).
fake_complexity: High. 'caustics', 'chromatic', 'refraction', 'parallax', 'magnet', 'cursorHighlight', 'lighting=iridescent|volumetric|caustic', 'border=particle|neon' all advertise effects that do nothing.
target: single Glass surface primitive (merge OptimizedGlassCore + GlassCore + OptimizedGlassAdvanced + GlassAdvanced; align with LiquidGlassMaterial)
justification: This is the de-facto material workhorse (~180 importers) and its core path — tokens via createGlassStyle — is the right one. But the public API is mostly decoration: more than a dozen props are accepted and ignored, the 'advanced' flags are data attributes pretending to be effects, the radius scale bypasses tokens, and auto-tier detection restyles every surface after hydration. In 5.0 it should be the one Glass surface: intent/elevation/radius/interactive only, properly typed polymorphism (or asChild via Slot), CSS-driven tier via @supports/media queries instead of post-mount JS, and the fake flags removed with a codemod.

name: Portal / GlassPortal
material_impl: n/a (headless)
a11y: Neutral. Fine.
api: children/container/forceMount. Correct mount-gate for SSR. forceMount naming diverges from Radix semantics (here it means 'render before mount', Radix uses it for presence). Not forwardRef (not needed).
ssr: Safe: returns null until mounted; document guarded.
duplicates: Direct createPortal(…, document.body) in GlassSelect.tsx:590, GlassActionSheet.tsx:340, GlassSpotlightSearch.tsx:458, GlassSidebar.tsx:402, GlassSelfHealingSystem.tsx:1315 — these bypass the primitive
justification: Small, correct, SSR-safe portal. The issue is adoption, not the code: several overlay components call createPortal directly against document.body, skipping the mount gate and any future shared layer/stacking container. Keep, and migrate those callers onto it (and onto a shared z-index layer root).

name: Positioner / GlassPositioner
material_impl: n/a (headless)
a11y: Neutral; exposes data-side/data-align for styling.
api: forwardRef; side/align/sideOffset/alignOffset/collisionPadding/strategy/contained. Missing vs Floating UI/Radix: no flip/shift-to-other-side (clamping only, so a 'top' popover near the top edge overlaps its anchor), no arrow, no size/available-height, no ResizeObserver on floating or anchor (only window resize/scroll + children change, :129-143), so content that changes size after async load is mispositioned. strategy='absolute' is wrong: it uses viewport getBoundingClientRect coordinates without adding scroll offset or subtracting the offsetParent rect (:98-117). `contained` simply disables positioning. Positions are set via React state on every scroll event (capture listener on window, :137) — re-render per scroll frame, no rAF throttle.
ssr: 'use client'; useLayoutEffect will warn under SSR in React 18 (:129). Initial -9999 offscreen position (:72-74).
fake_complexity: No, but 'collision' handling is just clamping.
duplicates: Bespoke getBoundingClientRect positioning in GlassTooltip.tsx, GlassPopover.tsx, GlassSelect.tsx, GlassMultiSelect.tsx, GlassContextMenu.tsx
target: @floating-ui/react-dom (useFloating with flip/shift/size/arrow + autoUpdate) wrapped as the library Positioner
justification: A premium overlay system lives or dies on positioning, and this is a minimal clamp-only implementation with a broken absolute strategy, no flip, no size observation, and per-scroll re-renders. Meanwhile tooltip/popover/select/context-menu each hand-roll their own positioning. Replace the internals with Floating UI behind the same Positioner API and migrate every overlay onto it.

name: RovingFocusGroup (Root/Item) / GlassRovingFocusGroup
tests: src/primitives/native-primitives.test.tsx:195, :215 (arrow keys, Home/End, disabled skip, RTL) — no assertion on tabIndex / tab-stop memory
material_impl: n/a (headless)
a11y: Arrow/Home/End/RTL handling is correct for the tested paths. Likely defect in tab-stop memory (reasoned from code, not executed): Item's register effect depends on `context` (:176-181), and the context value is re-memoized whenever currentTabStopId changes (:113-137). Every focus move therefore runs all Items' cleanups (unregisterItem nulls currentTabStopId if it was the focused id, :58-61) then re-registers them in order (registerItem sets current ?? id, :53-56), resetting the tab stop to the FIRST item. Effect: the focused item ends up with tabIndex=-1, and Tab-out/Shift-Tab-back always returns to item 1 — the core purpose of a roving tabindex. Also: item order is Map insertion order, not DOM order (:65), so dynamically inserted items navigate out of order; no typeahead; Item default element is a div with no role.
api: Compound object API (RovingFocusGroup.Root/.Item) plus named exports; forwardRef; asChild via Slot; orientation/loop/dir; no controlled currentTabStopId/onCurrentTabStopIdChange. Root passes role={props.role} then spreads props (redundant, :143-146).
duplicates: Hand-rolled arrow-key handling in GlassTabs.tsx, EnhancedGlassTabs.tsx, GlassToolbar.tsx, GlassMenuPrimitive.tsx, and GlassWorkspaceTabs (which has none)
justification: The right primitive to have, and keyboard movement works, but the register/unregister effect keyed on the whole context value likely breaks tab-stop persistence — the defining roving-tabindex behaviour — and the tests don't catch it. Fix by depending on stable callbacks only (split context into a stable dispatch context and a state context), order items by compareDocumentPosition, add controlled state and typeahead, add a tabIndex/Tab-return test, then make every tabs/toolbar/menu/radio-group in the library consume it.

name: Slot / GlassSlot
material_impl: n/a
a11y: Neutral.
api: forwardRef; merges className, style, composes handlers (child first, slot skipped if defaultPrevented) and refs. Gaps vs @radix-ui/react-slot: no Slottable support (cannot wrap icon + child), returns null silently for non-element/multiple children (:71-73, no dev warning), reads child.ref directly (:76) which warns under React 19 (peer range allows <20, package.json:376) — should read child.props.ref when available. composeRefs creates a new callback each render (ref churn).

justification: Compact and correct for the common case, with a real test. Polish for React 19 ref access, add Slottable and a dev warning for invalid children, then standardise every asChild-capable component on it.

name: GlassWorkspace

stories.note: No story for any workspace export; only registry recipes (src/registry/recipes.ts:978, 1096, 1713)

material_impl: Bespoke utility-class glass for the inspector <aside>: glass-border-white/12 glass-bg-white/10 glass-backdrop-blur-xl (:54) — hard-coded white-alpha, does not use createGlassStyle/OptimizedGlass tokens, so it will not follow intent/elevation/theme or the dark/light token system.
a11y: Inspector rendered as unlabeled <aside> (multiple unlabeled complementary landmarks when nested with GlassInspectorPanel, which is also an <aside> — the test composes exactly that, producing aside-in-aside).
api: forwardRef; className passthrough; header/commandDock/inspector slots. Layout is auto-fit minmax(28rem) grid (:46-47), so main/inspector ratio is uncontrolled and the inspector gets equal width with main; no collapse/resize. Overlaps GlassWorkflowShell, which uses GlassSplitPane instead — two layout strategies for the same thing in one file.
target: src/app-shell (GlassPage + GlassSplitPane + a single Inspector panel)
justification: Thin layout sugar over app-shell with bespoke white-alpha glass and an equal-width auto-fit grid that is not what a productivity workspace needs. Merge into app-shell as one workspace layout with a resizable/collapsible inspector built on the token material, and drop the duplicate layout path.

name: GlassWorkspaceHeader
material_impl: Delegates to GlassPageHeader; no own material.
a11y: Heading comes from GlassPageHeader (test asserts heading role).
api: forwardRef but the ref attaches to the wrapper div while all other props (including aria-*, data-*, id) go to GlassPageHeader and className goes to the wrapper (:70-78) — split prop routing is surprising.
duplicates: GlassPageHeader (src/app-shell/components.tsx:292) — this adds only a tabs slot
justification: Adds one slot to GlassPageHeader; fold it in as a prop.

name: GlassWorkspaceTabs / GlassWorkspaceTab
material_impl: Bespoke utility glass (glass-border-white/12 glass-bg-white/10 glass-backdrop-blur-xl, :99). Active tab uses glass-surface-primary/15 plus glass-border-sky-300/40 (:127) — the latter class does not exist in src/styles (rg -F 'glass-border-sky-300' src/styles -> 0), so the active border never renders.
a11y: Broken tab pattern: role=tablist/role=tab with aria-selected, but every tab is a normal button in tab order (no roving tabindex), no Arrow/Home/End handling (despite RovingFocusGroup existing in the same package), no aria-controls/tabpanel linkage. Focus ring classes focus-visible:glass-ring-2 / focus-visible:glass-ring-sky-300 / focus-visible:glass-outline-none (:125) have no CSS definitions (0 hits in src/styles), so keyboard focus relies on the UA default outline. Touch target ~ py-1.5 + text-sm ≈ 32px, below 44px.
api: Tabs declares value/onValueChange (:86-89) but never uses them — they are spread onto the <div> (:102), leaking `onValueChange` as an unknown DOM prop (React warning) and providing no selection state. Tab uses `active` boolean instead of value matching — inconsistent with GlassTabs.
fake_complexity: value/onValueChange imply a controlled tabs component that does not exist.
target: src/components/navigation/GlassTabs.tsx (one tabs implementation built on RovingFocusGroup)
justification: A third tabs implementation that advertises a controlled API it does not implement, fails the WAI-ARIA tabs keyboard pattern, references non-existent utility classes for its focus and active states, and leaks props to the DOM. Replace with the canonical GlassTabs.

name: GlassWorkspacePanel
material_impl: Bespoke white-alpha utility glass (:148). a11y: <section> with a visual title in a div, not a heading and not aria-labelledby — section without an accessible name is not a region landmark and screen-reader users lose the panel title as structure.
api: forwardRef, className, title/actions.
justification: Another panel with hand-written glass and broken header overrides; the library already has panel/card surfaces. Merge.

name: GlassWorkflowShell
material_impl: Composes app-shell GlassPage/GlassCommandDock/GlassSplitPane + GlassInspectorPanel; no own material.
a11y: Hard-coded English 'Inspector' heading (:282) — not localisable; inspector content placed inside a nameless aside.

target: app-shell workspace template (single layout with GlassWorkspace)
justification: A reasonable composition recipe, but it is a template, not a component, and conflicts with GlassWorkspace's layout. Keep one workspace template in app-shell (with i18n-able labels and resizable inspector) and present it in Storybook as a full-page pattern — that could become a real showcase once the material is token-driven.
